## F001: closed

`crates/daemon/src/community/directory.rs:141-148,1919-1942,2030-2071`

`finished_by` retains the selected holding's exact `from` in ReleaseTarget, alongside role, instance and seat. The project remains bound by the service call. Under the existing writer lock, `release_many` now requires that exact holding to remain open before changing it.

A release/reassignment between selection and the writer therefore cannot substitute a replacement row. The old pinned target is skipped and named; the replacement is not put into the commit or the store's ended-assignment update. The writer's lock surrounds the build/read-modify-write operation (`community/writer.rs:118-137`), so the new identity comparison is at the effective mutation boundary, not another earlier snapshot check.

Single release and release --batch deliberately construct `from: None` and preserve their existing current-open-row behavior (`community/directory.rs:1831-1837`; `http/directory.rs:1590-1595`). The new pin does not change their atomicity or CLI contract.

## Controlled proof and retained behavior

`a_reassignment_between_the_choice_and_the_commit_survives` drives the actual `finished_by` selection, then explicitly releases and reassigns coder/215 to the same seat before invoking `release_many` (`tests/directory_http.rs:6990-7059`). It requires:

- only reviewer/231 to end;
- the stale coder pin to be named;
- the replacement's complete store Assignment to remain unchanged;
- the committed coder document's newest row to remain open.

The store and committed-document checks are separate update paths, not two readings of the returned receipt. There is no timing-dependent race setup.

The coder reports the pin mutant killed: disabling identity protection ended two holdings where the regression expected one. The coder also confirmed the old 75271b1 interleaving defect and supplied the earlier drop-cutoff mutant failure. Those are author-run proofs; this reviewer ran no local tests.

The retained CI regressions still pass: reassignment followed by replay writes nothing; a retry after a refused writer release ends the original pre-merge holdings; missing merge time ends nothing and explains why. Batch all-or-nothing still passes.
